**Theorem and interpretation.** For every word generated by the original Farey recursion, each of its two standard and two alternate finite outputs, in its authentic restored physical frame, is the restriction up to an additive constant of its corresponding recurrent integer field on the F-lattice. The copies translated with the canonical deck jets cover the plane with consistent values, and the resulting global field has Laplacian in {−1,0}. This concerns the intended recursion on finite supports with integer arithmetic, no loss of translated sites, the original selected initializers, shifts, intermediate normalizations, and the exact order of its minima. It does not assert that every run of the distributed Julia program with a finite allocated buffer and floating-point arithmetic returns that mathematical output.

The short proof has two separate inductions. The difficult inputs in them are proved in the cited packets; they are not one-line observations about arbitrary minima. In particular, general recurrence neither survives arbitrary minima nor follows from prior parents being recurrent.

## 1. Construct the recurrent fields before reading the finite output

At a proper even child use the minimum M of its two genuine earlier parent sheets on its canonical fundamental polygon E. This M is already recurrent throughout the plane: under the *actual earlier* conjugate chart it is an integer-threshold minimum of the previously controlled chain pair. Sew the even fields at a fixed depth first; raw polygon conjugacy constructs the odd ones including the same-depth swapped-word sibling without assuming its recurrence.

Recurrence alone is not the induction hypothesis. Carry the true price strips and two extra zero levels, signed policies and their ranks, plus recurrence and clean burning for every integer threshold of the earlier chain. Price the new polygon by recurrent comparison against M; get the two extra zeros from the previous opposite parent. Build the contained unit-proof graph W1 from **earlier** ranks and the strengthened strips. Its graph/cut argument on the physical plane now gives signed strictly decreasing ranks for F. *After* rank, the full raw P and D comparisons on all kept edges pay the two-sheet chain and clean bands for the next generation. At a black site both physical inputs must be retained. The alternate H=ceil((F+F(·+sigma))/2) has its own decreasing lexicographic rank: first the parity of the genuine slip D, then the standard rank. At a minimum of that rank a finite forbidden set cannot meet its local quota. The odd companion transfers through the physical graph isomorphism and harmonic correction. This applies to all proper slopes: it is not a burn on a finite torus. Initial pure runs, including the actual zero-length common root, initialize the *full* invariant, not only the recurrence assertion.

## 3. Why this is physical recurrence, and distinct fields

The previously adopted actual domain theorem gives D_native+Lambda=Z² for EACH output individually, with Lambda generated by U=mu(d,n), V=(n−d,n+d), mu=2 for odd type and 1 for even. The whole-field agreement and the canonical deck laws prescribe the SAME value at each physical site regardless of which translated original native representative is used. These are the jets of the identified fields, not guessed independent constants for different copies. Where one wants the paper's existence of a compatible extension, these explicit laws construct it. If a different external program specifies a different constant character, equality to that different program is not asserted. Since the actual extension is the field from §1, it inherits its physical forbidden-set criterion even when no single native copy contains a full incoming star.

On this lattice the increment under translation by v has affine slope Mv, with M=−(n,−d)(n,−d)^T/T, T=d²+2dn−n². Indeed MU=0, MV=(n,−d); the dual's harmonic conversion has the matching Hessian by s(z)²−T(x²+2xy−y²)=2(nx−dy)². Subtract ½z^TMz and choose a real linear function matching the two remaining generator constants. The residual is bounded periodic. For even type, H−F has zero U increment and V increment −1. An integer affine difference with zero slope on (d,n) would have slope j(n,−d), hence V increment −jT, impossible as T>1. For nonbase odd type, in phase 0 compare its two conjugates at Jz; the shift 2(d,n) becomes +V of the dual, giving H_odd−F_odd increment −1. In phase 1 compare instead with the standard at z+Z: identify F_even(J(z+Z))=F_even(delta−J(z+Z)) by genuine reflection and the alternate with H_even there, with the common h0(z+Z). The shift 2(d,n) now becomes −V of the dual, giving +1, while both the unshifted and shifted standards have zero primary increment. Either sign excludes integer affine equivalence since the odd primary is twice an integer vector. Genuine odd pure initializers have the separately verified −1 primary jet. These establish distinctness, not a classification modulo arbitrary spatial translations.

Every reduced interior fraction occurs: the unimodular odd/even pair p,q splits its cone by 2p+q and p+q. Write a primitive interior vector ip+jq with coprime positive integers i,j. If i/j is 2 or 1 it is a child; otherwise its positive coordinates in the selected subcone are (i−2j,j), (i−j,2j−i), or (i,j−i) respectively (up to pair order). The sum strictly decreases. Start at the genuine endpoint vectors (1,0),(1,1). So the two integer recurrent physical odometers exist for every proper reduced fraction, not only words tested on a finite range.
